records.name: Brighton
longform: Looking for a therapist in Brighton is easier than in most towns of its size, and harder than it looks. There are a lot of practitioners, spread between the city centre, Hove, Kemptown and the villages along the Downs. Parking near the seafront is expensive and slow. Most people choose somewhere on a bus route or within a short walk of Brighton or Hove station, and many therapists offer early morning or evening hours because so many clients commute to London.

Brighton has two universities and a large student population, which means there are practitioners who work a great deal with people in their late teens and twenties. It also has a long-established LGBTQ+ community, and a number of therapists say plainly on their profiles that this is where much of their work sits. The creative and digital industries are a large local employer, and freelancers and people between contracts make up a noticeable part of many caseloads.

Online sessions are common here. Some people choose them because a lunchtime slot from a shared flat or a co-working space is easier than a journey across the city. Others start online with a therapist in Brighton and move to the room later, or keep working online when they leave for a job elsewhere. If the therapist you want to see is in Hove and you are in Saltdean, online may be the difference between going and not going.

records.name: Manchester
longform: Manchester is well served for therapy, but the choice is spread across a wide area. Practitioners work from rooms in the city centre, in Didsbury, Chorlton, Prestwich and the towns of the wider conurbation. The tram makes a lot of them reachable without a car, and many therapists deliberately keep their rooms near a Metrolink stop for that reason. Driving into the centre for a weekday afternoon slot is the option most people regret.

The city has one of the largest student populations in Europe, several large hospitals, and a media and technology sector that has grown quickly over the last decade. Those three things shape who is looking for therapy here: students far from home, shift workers with unpredictable hours, and people in fast-moving jobs who find it hard to hold a regular weekly slot. Some therapists here offer fortnightly sessions or fixed short-term contracts for exactly that reason.

Online counselling is a normal part of the picture. If you live in Stockport or Bolton and the therapist you want is in Chorlton, an online session removes a journey that would otherwise decide the matter. Some people also prefer it because they do not want to be seen walking into a familiar building. Neither choice is better; it depends on you, your home and what you can keep up for as long as it is useful.
